notes:
CRM notes from discovery + workshop. Short bullets and call fragments below.

- Company: Elmwood Reserve Planning (payment/settlement platform for mid-size banks). Heavy PII, regulated EU and NA traffic.
- Primary ask: dedicated capacity with throughput guarantees and predictable unit economics for customer-facing chat assistant + background reranking pipeline.
- Security: must be able to prove SOC2 + ISO27001, KMS integration, audit logs for all inference calls, and ability to segregate EU tokens to EU region (data residency).
- Quote from CTO: 'We need predictable latency under load — financial customers won't tolerate 2s tail latencies during settlement windows.'
- Cost sensitivity: high; prefers committed reserved capacity to optimize unit cost, but wants burst capacity for marketing peaks.
- Procurement: legal wants 12-month SLA with credits and incident response matrix; finance pushing for blended ARR cap.
- Observability ask: per-route token cost, p50/p90/p99 latency by model, and per-request tracing to map back to call IDs.
- POC plan agreed: 6-week sizing pilot -> canary traffic (5%) -> full migration; will provide sample traffic logs for sizing.
- Internal stakeholders: CTO (Sarah Lowe), Head of Platform (Jamal Ortiz), Security Lead (Marta Kovac).
- Comments: SE workshop went deep on batch sizes and KV cache hit rates — they were surprised by the impact of prefix caching on effective QPS.

sizing_findings: Workload split: 60% background reranking (batchable), 40% user-facing chat/assist (latency sensitive).
Observed sample traffic (provided by Elmwood): steady-state QPS ~25 across business hours, peak burst QPS observed up to 220 (marketing/settlement spikes).
Average tokens/request: 180 tokens for chat (includes prompt + generation). Reranking average token footprint: ~60 tokens per candidate * 5 candidates => 300 tokens but highly batchable.
Baseline tokens/sec requirement (steady-state): ~4,500 tokens/sec. Peak burst tokens/sec: ~39,600 tokens/sec (220 QPS * 180 tokens).
Target latency SLOs: p50 < 200ms for routing/overhead, p95 < 700ms for chat end-to-end (<=512 tokens), p99 < 1.2s; reranking p95 < 1.5s allowed if batched offline windows used.
GPU sizing (initial estimate): reserved pool sized for steady-state: 16 x A100-80GB (or equivalent). To meet peak SLOs with <1.2s p99 need burst pool -> additional 12 GPUs (total burst-capable 28).

Autoscaling policy recommended: reserved pool handles steady traffic; burst pool on-demand with warm standby instances (pre-warmed models) to avoid cold-start latency >1s. Maintain 10% headroom for sudden settlement-window spikes.
Caching strategy: prefix/KV caching projected to reduce effective tokens/sec for repeat sessions by ~18-25% after warm-up; recommended cache TTLs and eviction tied to session affinity for chat flows.
Batching guidance: reranking jobs should be routed to a dedicated batch queue with continuous batching window 50-150ms to maximize GPU utilization while keeping SLAs acceptable.
sla_discussion: Elmwood requires 12-month SLA with 99.9% availability for dedicated control plane and 99.5% for GPU availability given maintenance windows.
Incident response: P1 response <1 hour, remediation timeline and credit tiers requested (legal wants example clause).

Performance guarantee: Redwood to guarantee p95 latency target for specified model family under committed QPS; fallback policy if backend cannot meet SLO (auto-route to lower-capacity model with notification).
Data residency clause: must ensure EU traffic served from EU region; audit logs with 1-year retention and exportable compliance reports.
risk_and_blockers: Procurement: Elmwood legal pushing for indemnity adjustments and SLA credit caps — delay until Redwood legal sign-off.
Residency evidence: Security team wants runbook and proof of isolated EU tenancy before signing.
Budget cadence: CFO requires a capital commitment approval cycle aligned to fiscal Q2 (decision gating GPU commit).
